Assumption 1 (Smoothness of the Upper- and Lower-Level Objective Functions) . The upper- and lower-level objective functions $f$ and $g$ are twice differentiable, and there exist positive constants $
u,\ell,ho$ , such that for any $z=(x,y)$ and $z^{\prime}=(x^{\prime},y^{\prime})$ , it holds that: $\displaystyle|f(z)-f(z^{\prime})|\leq
u\|z-z^{\prime}\|,\,\,\,\,\,\,\|
abla f(z)-
abla f(z^{\prime})\|\leq\ell\|z-z^{\prime}\|,$ $\displaystyle\|
abla g(z)-
abla g(z^{\prime})\|\leq\ell\|z-z^{\prime}\|,\,\,\,\,\,\,\|
abla^{2}g(z)-
abla^{2}g(z^{\prime})\|\leqho\|z-z^{\prime}\|,$ where $\|\cdot\|$ denotes Euclidean and spectral norm for vectors and matrices hereafter, respectively.

Definition 1 (First- and Second-Order Stationary Point) . Suppose Assumption 1 holds, and let $\lambda_{\min}(\cdot)$ denote the minimal eigenvalue of a matrix. For any given $x\in\mathbb{R}^{p}$ and any positive $\epsilon$ , 1. $y$ is a first-order stationary point (FOSP) if $
abla_{y}g(x,y)=0$ . It is an $\epsilon$ -FOSP if $\|
abla_{y}g(x,y)\|\leq\epsilon$ . 2. $y$ is a second-order stationary point (SOSP) if $
abla_{y}g(x,y)=0$ and $\lambda_{\min}(
abla^{2}_{yy}g(x,y))\geq 0$ . It is an $\epsilon$ -SOSP if $\|
abla_{y}g(x,y)\|\leq\epsilon$ and $\lambda_{\min}(
abla^{2}_{yy}g(x,y))\geq-\sqrt{ho\epsilon}$ .

Definition 2 (Local Minimum and Saddle Point) . Suppose that $g$ is differentiable. For any given $x\in\mathbb{R}^{p}$ , $y$ is a local minimum if $\nabla_{y}g(x,y)=0$ and there exists $\delta>0$ such that $g(x,y)\leq g(x,y^{\prime})$ for all $y^{\prime}\in\mathbb{B}_{y}(\delta)$ , where $\mathbb{B}_{y}(\delta)$ denotes an open ball of radius $\delta$ centered at $y$ . In contrast, $y$ is a saddle point if $\nabla_{y}g(x,y)=0$ and it is not a local minimum.

Definition 3 ( $\mu$ -Augmented Hypergradient-Based Convergence Metric) . Suppose $y$ is an $\epsilon^{\prime}$ -SOSP for a given $x$ (as defined in Def. 1 ) and all saddle points are strict. For any positive $\epsilon,\mu=\sqrt{\rho\epsilon^{\prime}}+\sigma$ , $(x,y)$ is said to be an $(\epsilon,\mu)$ -stationary solution to Eq. 2 if it satisfies: $\Pi(x,y):=\|\nabla\Phi_{\mu}(x)\|^{2}+\epsilon^{\prime}\leq\epsilon$ .

Theorem 1 . By selecting $K_{t}=\widetilde{\Theta}\big((t+1)^{\frac{8}{5}}\big)$ , $\sigma_{t}=\Theta\big((t+1)^{-p}\big)$ and $\alpha_{t}=\Theta\big((t+1)^{-q}\big)$ with $p\in(0,\frac{1}{3}),3p\leq q<1$ , for any $\delta\in(0,1)$ , with probability at least $1-\delta$ , the sequence $\{x_{t},y_{t}\}_{t}$ generated by Algorithm 1 satisfies the following convergence guarantee: $\min_{\frac{T}{2}\leq t\leq T}\Pi(x_{t},y_{t})=\mathcal{O}(\frac{1}{T^{1-q}}+\frac{1}{T^{2p}}+\frac{1}{T^{\frac{4}{5}}})$ . By selecting $(p,q)=(\frac{1}{5},\frac{3}{5})$ , we have $\min_{\frac{T}{2}\leq t\leq T}\Pi(x_{t},y_{t})=\mathcal{O}\big(T^{-\frac{2}{5}}\big)$ .

Theorem 2 (Formally restated Theorem 1 ) . By selecting parameters as follows: $\displaystyle\sigma_{t}=\Theta\left((t+1)^{-p}\right),\,\,\,\,\,\,\epsilon_{t}=\frac{\sigma_{t}^{4}}{\rho},\,\,\,\,\,\,\mu_{t}=\sqrt{\rho\epsilon_{t}}+\sigma_{t},\,\,\,\,\,\,\alpha_{t}=\Theta\left((t+1)^{-q}\right),\,\,\,\,\,\,\beta_{t}=\Theta\left(\frac{1}{\ell}\right),$ $\displaystyle N_{t}=\widetilde{\Theta}((t+1)^{\frac{p}{2}}),\,\,\,\,\,\,K_{t}=\widetilde{\Theta}((t+1)^{8p}),$ $\displaystyle\delta^{\prime}\in(0,\frac{1}{T}),\,\,\,\,\,\,\Delta_{g,t}\geq g(x_{t},y_{t})-\inf_{y}g(x_{t},y),\,\,\,\,\,\,\chi_{t}=3\max\left\{\log\left(\frac{q\ell\Delta_{g,t}}{\epsilon_{t}^{2}\delta^{\prime}}\right),4\right\},$ $\displaystyle r_{t}=\Theta\left(\frac{\epsilon_{t}}{\ell\chi_{t}^{2}}\right),\,\,\,\,\,\,\varrho_{t}=\Theta\left(\frac{\epsilon_{t}}{\chi_{t}^{2}}\right),\,\,\,\,\,\,\Delta_{G,t}=\Theta\left(\frac{\epsilon_{t}^{1.5}}{\chi_{t}^{3}\rho^{0.5}}\right),\,\,\,\,\,\,\Delta_{K,t}=\Theta\left(\frac{\ell\chi_{t}}{\rho^{0.5}\epsilon_{t}^{0.5}}\right),$ for any $\delta=T\delta^{\prime}\in(0,1)$ , $p\in(0,\frac{1}{3})$ , $3p\leq q<1$ , the sequence $\{x_{t},y_{t}\}_{t}$ generated by Algorithm 1 satisfies the following convergence guarantee w.p. $1-\delta$ : $\displaystyle\min_{\frac{T}{2}\leq t\leq T}\Pi(x_{t},y_{t})=\mathcal{O}\left(\frac{1}{T^{1-q}}+\frac{1}{T^{2p}}+\frac{1}{T^{\frac{4}{5}}}\right).$ When selecting $p=\frac{1}{5}$ and $q=\frac{3}{5}$ , we have $\min_{\frac{T}{2}\leq t\leq T}\Pi(x_{t},y_{t})=\mathcal{O}\left(T^{-\frac{2}{5}}\right)$ .

Corollary 1 . Whenever the lower-level local minimum satisfies the local curvature condition $
abla_{yy}^{2}g(x,y)\succeq\mu_{0}I_{q}$ for some $\mu_{0}>0$ , the bias bound yields $\|
abla\Phi_{\mu}(x)-
abla\Phi_{0}(x)\|=\mathcal{O}(\mu)$ . Combining this bound with the parameter selection in Theorem 1 gives: $\min_{\lceil T/2ceil\leq t\leq T}\|
abla\Phi_{0}(x_{t})\|^{2}=\mathcal{O}(T^{-2/5}).$
